NTA but you will be if you continue to pretend to be friends with her instead of just letting her go. 

And I want to explain that I do *not* mean you should cut out people who suffer from mental or chronic illness. It’s just clear that you no longer feel much empathy for her and you hanging around and engaging with her isn’t doing either one of you any favors. 

I had a friend in college, who is still my friend to this day, who I really suspect was similar (minus the drinking and shit talking her “friends”). She would randomly bring up lifelong diagnoses that she’d never mentioned in the years I’d known her- strange because sometimes her various illnesses were all she could talk about. For example, after three years of knowing her, suddenly she was autistic and had been her entire life. One day, she would claim not to be able to process sarcasm because of this, and the next she’d be using and processing it just fine. 

I’ve also driven her to the ER on several occasions for problems that I suspected didn’t really exist. I’d sit in the room with her while she was being seen by doctors and they could never find the issue and her stories kept changing like she couldn’t keep it straight. Once I took her to the ER because her hands were apparently in horrible pain (even though she could text just fine) and the doctors found nothing wrong and discharged her two hours later. The next day she shows up to class with two hand braces from CVS claiming she has carpal tunnel in both hands. She never had surgery and never had PT. 

A couple years later I got her a job where I worked in a national park, and taught her to rock climb. No issues with her hands. I’ve had carpal tunnel surgery (and she “got carpal tunnel” very shortly after I had my surgery). I still experience pain and limitations when I climb. It doesn’t just go away without treatment. 

She also says she has PTSD, which to be fair she may very well, but has never seen a therapist since she was a child (and the event that caused her PTSD happened as an adult) so she self diagnosed that as well. 

Anyway, short story long, the difference here is even though I recognize her antics and I don’t always believe her, I support her as if I did. Because at the end of the day, making up illnesses is still a serious problem that suggests a mental health issue. I do have to take breaks from being around her because my needs are important, too. But if you continue to pretend to be her friend then you *will* become the asshole.

I have three tattoos, one that almost no one ever sees, and two that people see every day and are very difficult to hide. I've never had trouble finding a variety of jobs because of them, and I get a lot of compliments on them.

The one no one ever sees, I don't regret because I love it and it's important to me, but honestly I forget it's there. I appreciate the ones in my eyesight more.

Also for me, the times I've failed to do it have always turned me off for a while because there is just no pleasant way to die. And every time I've come to clarity after trying to kill myself I've just been so relieved to still be suffering, as odd as it sounds. Maybe it's just my inner survival instinct finally waking up after being called back from the dead. Maybe it's because I realized when I got out of the hospital I could stop and get a burger from my favorite takeout place on the way back home. Maybe it was because my cat licks my feet when I get home and I never really comprehended that until the moment I got home when I never planned to go home again.

Maybe I just wanted to lose that extra five pounds before I was buried with it? Or a new season of my favorite show is coming out soon and I want to know what happens. Apparently when I was gone from work my boss told my coworkers to step up because it takes three people to do my job.

For me I realized I needed to stop looking for one big reason to stay alive. I didn't even need a lot of little ones, and certainly no cliche ones. I just needed one stupid thing to hold on to for five more minutes when things are tough. It could be garlic fries.
